newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat jointing ahead of average.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat jointing ahead of average.

text.p: Warm weather during the week ended Sunday boosted wheat growth and allowed jointing to advance ahead of average, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop weather report.
Warmer weather and high winds helped dry out saturated soils in many parts of the state. Soil moisture levels were adequate to surplus in most areas.
Oklahoma wheat condition was rated 15 percent excellent, 68 good, 14 fair and three poor. That compared to last week's rating of nine percent excellent, 74 good, 14 fair and three percent poor.

Wheat acreage jointing was reported at 19 percent, versus three percent in 1996 and 15 percent for the five-year average. The report said producers were actively preparing ground for summer crops, although wet fields have slowed activities in many areas.

Pasture conditions improved slightly with the warmer temperatures and were rated three percent excellent, 49 good, 38 fair, nine poor and one very poor. That compared to the previous week's rating of three percent excellent, 46 good, 41 fair, nine poor and one very poor.
Insect pressure was reported to be light statewide.
